newsitem.title: USA: BMW, Lexus top luxury car crash test, US group says.
newsitem.headline: BMW, Lexus top luxury car crash test, US group says.

text.p: BMW's 5 Series and the Lexus LS 400 earned the best overall ratings in a survey of six 1997 large luxury cars, the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety said on Wednesday.
The Mercedes E Class and the Lincoln Continental earned acceptable evaluations, while the Infiniti Q45 was marginal and the Cadillac Seville received a poor evaluation, it said.
"Given the high prices of these models, you should expect superior protection in a crash, and the BMW and Lexus came through," institute President Brian O'Neill said.

Institute researchers used 40 mph offset crash tests to evaluate how well vehicle structure manages the energy of the crash, injury risk measured using a dummy, and how well dummy movement is controlled during impact.

The Mercedes performance was marred by the opening of the driver door during the crash, while the forces on the dummy's left lower leg in the Lincoln were high enough to break a driver's leg, the institute said.
The Infiniti crash test resulted in possible head injury, while there was compacting of the driver space in the Cadillac, which has the oldest design of the group.
"Expensive cars like the ones the institute tested are those in which state-of-the-art safetly designs and technologies typically are introduced," O'Neill said.

The four imported models come with side airbags, and safety belt tensioners to reduce seat belt slack. Front airbags in the BMW and Mercedes have higher deployment thresholds for belted occupants. These features are not yet found in most popular models, he said.

The BMW is made by BMW, the Lexus by Toyota Motor Corp, the Mercedes by Daimler-Benz AG'S Mercedes division, the Infiniti by Nissan Motor Co, the Lincoln by Ford Motor Co and the Cadillac by General Motors Corp.
